title: Publish the Clinical Hospital Rotation Cohort Management Blueprint for Nursing and Medical Academies, by Fri 18 Dec
description:
Medical, nursing, and healthcare training institutions place students into rotational hospital ward cohorts (internal medicine, pediatrics, surgery) where rapid peer communication, shift handover logs, and clinical case discussions must occur without violating patient confidentiality. Fragmented SMS and consumer messaging tools create compliance risks and lost handovers. This blueprint establishes Zedu as a structured, privacy-conscious workspace for hospital clinical placements.

Work under this goal:
- Build the hospital ward clinical rotation channel architecture: private ward rotation pods (#ward-surgery-alpha, #ward-pediatrics), clinical preceptor supervision channels (#preceptor-sos), and cross-shift announcements.
- Author the 15-minute daily shift-handover and clinical debrief protocol using native Zedu Buzz audio sessions with host moderation controls.
- Design clinical logbook submission and peer case presentation guidelines using Zedu's 440px threaded discussion drawer to structure diagnostic Q&A without patient-identifiable data.
- Draft the preceptor evaluation rubric and student ward competency checklist shared via Zedu File Management with view-only permissions.

Done when: A turnkey healthcare rotation operations manual is published with shift-handover run sheets, clinical ward channel taxonomy, confidentiality guidelines, and preceptor evaluation rubrics verified against production zedu.chat features.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Make "no patient identifiers" the first rule, with a de-identification template, and state Zedu isn't a clinical record system
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The biggest risk in rotation chat is patient data. Approach: before any channel design, write the rule that no names, record numbers, dates of birth, photos of charts or faces are posted, with a fill-in template for case discussions (age band, presenting problem, findings, question) and an example. State plainly that Zedu isn't a medical record or handover system of record, and confirm with the team whether the terms allow health information at all. Handover logs stay in the hospital's system; Zedu holds learning discussion only. Done: the rule, the template, the team's confirmed position, and the channel layout that follows from it.

upvotes.reason: "Make "no patient identifiers" the first rule, with a de-identification template, and state Zedu isn't a clinical record system" has a scriptable structure, so it can be produced and reviewed rather than left open-ended. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.
Patient identifiers turn a teaching tool into a clinical-data risk. Putting de-identification first, and stating Zedu is not a clinical record system, is the right order.
A no-identifiers rule and a de-identification template are the gating safety requirement for clinical rotation chat, and stating Zedu is not a record system sets the boundary.
A clear no-patient-identifiers rule plus a de-identification template is the minimum safeguard for hospital rotations, and stating Zedu is not a clinical record system sets the boundary.

This is a necessary safety boundary for a clinical-rotation blueprint: it keeps identifiable patient records out of Zedu, uses only de-identified learning discussions, and requires the team to confirm whether health information is allowed before the workflow is designed. The scope should remain a learning discussion space, not a clinical handover system.
